title: Reoperative CABG strategies: preoperative imaging, sternal re-entry, conduit management and embolization prevention
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 111 (Reoperative Coronary Artery Surgery)
STS Clinical Practice Guidelines on Arterial Conduits and Reoperations

steps.say: Preoperative evaluation for redo cardiac surgery requires mandatory high-resolution chest computed tomography. Axial imaging clearly depicts the retrosternal space, proximity of the ascending aorta, and location of patent internal mammary artery grafts. Measuring the distance between the sternum and underlying structures prevents fatal lacerations.
steps.tx: Meticulous operative planning for **reoperative surgery** mandates a non-contrast or contrast-enhanced **chest CT** scan to delineate the **retrosternal space**. Cross-sectional imaging quantifies the exact distance between the posterior sternal cortex, ascending aorta, right ventricle, and patent coronary bypass conduits before sternal re-entry.

vis.caption: Cross-sectional and radiographic retrosternal evaluation prior to redo sternotomy. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Chest radiograph and computed tomography illustrating retrosternal clearance.

steps.say: Lacerating a patent internal mammary artery graft during sternotomy causes catastrophic anterior wall infarction. Inadvertent injury to a patent LIMA graft leads to sudden ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest. Reported perioperative mortality from this complication exceeds thirty to fifty percent.
steps.tx: Inadvertent **patent LIMA injury** during **sternal re-entry** causes immediate, massive anteroseptal myocardial ischemia and refractory **ventricular fibrillation**. Uncontrolled hemorrhage and loss of anterior perfusion carry an operative mortality exceeding 30 to 50 percent, emphasizing extreme vigilance during anterior chest opening.

left.title: Patent LIMA Characteristics
points: Maintains critical blood supply to anterior myocardium
Extremely vulnerable to oscillating saw injury
Inadvertent laceration leads to refractory arrest

right.title: Preventive Strategies
points: Preoperative CT mapping of internal mammary course
Peripheral cannulation on standby before saw entry
Strict oscillating saw control on anterior cortex only

steps.say: Establish peripheral femoral-femoral bypass before sternotomy whenever high-risk adhesions are present. When a patent graft adheres directly beneath the sternal midline, peripheral cannulation permits rapid decompression and hypothermic cooling. Decompressing the heart moves cardiac structures away from the posterior sternal plate.
steps.tx: When preoperative imaging reveals dense **retrosternal adhesion** or a midline-crossing graft, elective **femoral-femoral bypass** is established prior to sternal division. Circulatory support enables rapid cardiac decompression, ventricular volume unloading, and protective **hypothermic cooling** before dividing dense retrosternal fibrous scar tissue.

nodes.label: CT reveals graft or aorta adhered directly to posterior sternum
Expose common femoral artery and vein under local or general anesthesia
Cannulate and initiate peripheral femoral-femoral cardiopulmonary bypass
Decompress cardiac chambers and proceed with safe sternal division

steps.say: Sternal re-entry requires an oscillating saw rather than a standard reciprocating saw. The surgeon divides the anterior cortex completely under direct vision, followed by gentle upward retraction of the bone edges. Dividing the posterior cortex with fine dissection against the posterior periosteum protects adherent tissues.
steps.tx: Sternal re-entry utilizes an **oscillating saw** to divide the **anterior cortex** cleanly without penetrating deep mediastinal tissues. The sternal halves are elevated gently with bone hooks, allowing the surgeon to divide the posterior cortical bone and dissect strictly along the **posterior periosteum** under direct illumination.

rows: Gentle bone hook elevation and saw
Ensures direct visualization of underlying scar plane
Maintains plane on periosteum away from cardiac chambers

steps.say: Limit mediastinal dissection strictly to what is necessary for cannulation and grafting. Extensive adhesiolysis causes major bleeding and risks injuring cardiac chambers. Selective dissection focused only on cannulation sites, aortic cross-clamping, and coronary targets improves outcomes.
steps.tx: Adopting **selective dissection** with **minimal adhesiolysis** is a core principle in redo surgery. Dissection is strictly confined to targeted **cannulation sites**, aortic cross-clamp application areas, and distal coronary targets, leaving non-essential dense pericardial adhesions undisturbed to reduce bleeding and operative trauma.

left.title: Selective Dissection Approach
points: Frees only aorta, right atrium, and target vessels
Minimizes blood loss and coagulopathic bleeding
Shortens operative and cardiopulmonary bypass times

right.title: Complete Adhesiolysis Pitfalls
points: Causes extensive raw surface microvascular bleeding
Risks tearing thin-walled right atrium or ventricle
Increases transfusion requirements and lung injury

steps.say: A patent internal mammary artery requires temporary clamping during cardioplegic arrest. Leaving the LIMA unclamped allows warm systemic blood to enter the left anterior descending artery, washing out cold cardioplegia. Clamping the LIMA ensures consistent hypothermic arrest and anterior wall protection.
steps.tx: When a patent internal mammary artery graft is present, mandatory **LIMA clamping** is performed synchronously with aortic cross-clamping. Unclamped mammary flow permits continuous warm systemic blood delivery that causes **cardioplegia washout**, resulting in persistent myocardial electrical activity and compromised **anterior wall protection**.

nodes.label: Dissect patent LIMA pedicle near chest wall entry
Apply soft vascular bulldog clamp upon aortic cross-clamping
Deliver antegrade or retrograde hypothermic cardioplegia
Release LIMA clamp immediately upon cross-clamp removal

steps.say: Old degenerated saphenous vein grafts contain highly friable atherosclerotic debris. Manipulating diseased vein grafts before cross-clamping dislodges plaque and causes atheroembolism into the coronary bed. Dissect new bypass targets first and avoid touching old vein grafts.
steps.tx: Atherosclerotic old vein grafts contain friable, unorganized necrotic debris and mural thrombus. Touching or manipulating a **friable vein graft** prior to aortic cross-clamping risks dislodging catastrophic **atheroembolism** into the distal coronary **microcirculation**, precipitating irreversible refractory myocardial infarction and profound intraoperative ventricular collapse.

rows: Dissect remote from old vein course
Ligate graft after completing new distal anastomoses

steps.say: Ligate old, failing vein grafts after completing new distal bypasses. Leaving diseased old conduits open allows competitive flow and risks future thromboembolism. Surgical graft ligation eliminates these hazards while securing sole antegrade flow through new grafts.
steps.tx: Definitive **graft ligation** of diseased or failing prior conduits is carried out immediately after establishing new bypasses. Tying off old degenerated grafts eliminates **competing flow** against the new conduit and permanently abolishes the nidus for **recurrent embolization** into the coronary vasculature.

vis.caption: Surgical inspection and conduit management during complex redo revascularization. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Clinical illustration demonstrating conduit ligation and revascularization inspection.
